questions.question:
You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Read this email from your English-speaking friend, Alex, and the notes you have made.

From: Alex
Subject: Guess what!

Hi!

I've got some great news: I've found a flat to rent, and it's in your neighbourhood! I'm moving in at the end of next month. (Note 1: Great!)

I don't know the area at all yet. What's the best thing about living there? (Note 2: Tell Alex)

I'll need to do a lot of shopping for the flat. Where do you think I should go? (Note 3: Suggest…)

And would you like to help me on moving day? I'll buy you lunch! (Note 4: Yes, but…)

See you soon,
Alex

Write your email to Alex using all the notes.
questions.explanation: A good answer is an informal email of about 100 words that covers all four notes: reacts with pleasure to Alex's news (Great!), describes the best thing about the neighbourhood with a reason (Tell Alex), suggests a place to shop for the flat and says why (Suggest…), and agrees to help on moving day while adding a condition or problem, for example a time when you are busy (Yes, but…). It should open and close like an email to a friend and use linking words such as because, so and but.

questions.question:
Choose ONE of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Question A: Article
You see this notice on an English-language website for teenagers.

Articles wanted!
My ideal home
Where would your ideal home be? What would it look like, and what would you have in it? Why would it be perfect for you?
The best articles will be published on our website.

Write your article.

Question B: Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
The old house at the end of the street was finally sold.

Write your story.
questions.explanation: Article: a good answer has an interesting title, speaks directly to the reader, and answers all the questions in the notice: where the ideal home would be, what it would look like and contain, and why it would be perfect, using the second conditional (it would have…, I would…). Story: a good answer begins with the given sentence, has a clear sequence of events and a satisfying ending, and uses past tenses and time linkers (at first, then, suddenly, in the end). Both answers should be about 100 words.
